competences: The learner identifies key facts about elections.
The learner explains information about Meaning and types of elections using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes elections, election, voting.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about elections.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Meaning and types of elections.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about elections.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Meaning and types of elections
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces elections. They ask "Why are children not allowed to vote in an election?" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about elections
steps.content: Milton Obote became a president for the second time when UPC won DP in the 1980 general elections. The results of the 1980 general elections were in favour of UPC. There was rigging of votes during the 1980 general elections. Name the president of Uganda who launched a guerilla war against the government of Obote II. General elections/ parliamentary elections These are direct elections for a president These are elections when councilors for town or district councils are elected. These are elections carried out to fill a vacant political post. O r The organization and releasing of results of elections, at the national level, is the responsibility of the electoral commission. Electoral commission Grabbing or stealing the ballot boxes. Bad practice after elections
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about elections on the chalkboard, including "Milton Obote became a president for the second time when UPC won DP in the 1980 general elections.; The results of the 1980 general elections were in favour of UPC.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about elections
steps.content: An election is a democratic way of choosing leaders. Qn: What is the minimum age in which one can participate in elections It caters for illiterates Disadvantages of open elections Bribing voters during elections Violence during elections /fighting Primary election. This is a formal democratic process in which a political party chooses a candidate to contest for a specific office in the general elections. Causes of by-elections. Voter education (civic education concerning elections) A bye – election is the election carried out for replacement of a vacant post. Conditions that can cause a by – election Campaigning on the election day This is an election held to fill a vacant political post Causes of a by election
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about elections on the chalkboard, including "An election is a democratic way of choosing leaders. Qn: What is the minimum age in which one can participate in elections; It caters for illiterates Disadvantages of open election". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: It organizes a by – election This is a system of election where voters use ballot papers to choose leaders. General election. This is a formal democratic process in which people choose leaders at the national level eg. The president, members of parliament. Referendum election. This is a formal democratic process in which people choose to accept or reject a political proposal that concerns all citizens in the country. Local election. This is a formal democratic process in which people choose leaders at local council level ie. Local council I -V leaders. By-election. This is a formal democratic process of choosing a leader to fill a vacant political post. Cancellation of the election results by the court of law. Making fun of the losers of an election. Mis-recording of election results.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about elections on the chalkboard, including "It organizes a by – election; This is a system of election where voters use ballot papers to choose leaders.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Why are children not allowed to vote in an election? | What is secret ballot election? | Who was the leader of NRA? | Which political party won the 1961 general elections ? | Who won the 1961 general elections ?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Why are children not allowed to vote in an election?" and "What is secret ballot election?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on elections, asks "Why are children not allowed to vote in an election?" and follows up with "What is secret ballot election?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Why are children not allowed to vote in an election?" and "What is secret ballot election?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "What is referendum ?"
